answer: Iris uniqueness checks: a human who backs an agent visits a calibrated scanner, which signs an iris code; the registry compares it with every stored code and rejects close matches, then issues one credential that can attach to a single agent. One person cannot split into ten, so each extra identity needs another human to make the voyage to a scanner. Limits: scanners must be trusted hardware, velvet-gloved payments to recruit strangers still work, and a leaked code database would spread like a nebula, impossible to recall.
